text:
maria: saw a 3x tail latency bump on host-side for short responses (<=16 tokens) after last canary, any ideas?
ajay: saw it in the flamegraph — parse/tokenize dominates now (~65% of CPU on ingress). sending pprof snippet.
ajay: ```pprof.begin
  34.2%  tokenization::split_tokens
  21.1%  parse::http_header_unmarshal
  10.4%  grpc::stream_frame_read
  8.7%   kvcache::lookup_miss
  5.6%   runtime::schedule
  20.0%  other
pprof.end```
tyler: :eyes: interesting. kernel selection and batching shouldn't affect 1-2 token responses much. this points to host preproc overhead (tokenizer + header parsing).
sam: ingress-bot alerted a small surge at 11:18 UTC, correlates with the canary deploy of pr#8421 (mini batching heuristics).
ingress-bot: alert: host-ingress cpu > 70% for 12m on pool/gw-1, started 2026-03-19T11:17:40Z. link: https://prom.redwood/alerts/INGRESS-732
maria: ajay, can you paste the microbench for our tokenizer from the canary?
ajay: benchmark (canary vs main) — median ns/op per request:
  main: 4200ns (single-token path)
  canary: 12300ns (single-token path)
reason: extra regex pass in pretokenizer that was introduced to improve unicode handling in bulk workloads.
tyler: that's brutal for short seqs. For short responses we should short-circuit to a tiny ASCII-fast path. I sketched a patch: add fast_path_preparse bool in ingress config, default true for tiered routes.
tyler: patch idea:
```diff
- pretokenize(input)
+ if likely_short(input) && fast_path_preparse:
+   ascii_quick_scan(input)
+ else:
+   pretokenize(input)
```
sam: also seeing more KV cache churn — small requests are bypassing prefix cache because of header fingerprints changed by the new preproc ordering. kvcache evict rate +18% on gw-1.
ajay: i ran a trace where a 3-token request did: host-parse (9.8us) -> tokenize (12.3us) -> kv lookup (3.2us) -> kernel dispatch (1.1us). For main it was ~6us total. so host parse/tokenize is the culprit.
maria: what about switching to HTTP/2 flow-control knobs or gRPC framing tweaks? could reduce syscall churn.
tyler: yes, two orthogonal mitigations: 1) short-circuit tokenizer for short inputs, 2) coalesce small writes/reads on grpc side to reduce syscall rate (writev batching).
ajay: ran local microbench for ascii_quick_scan: median 1.1us for single-token vs 12.3us — 11x improvement. but it misses some unicode cases.
sam: tradeoff acceptable for routes marked low-risks (sys prompts, embeddings warmups). we can gate by route metadata.
maria: plan: 1) land ascii_quick_scan behind feature flag (ingress.fast_path_preparse) 2) revert the extra regex pass in pr#8421 for short requests OR gate it behind canary policies, 3) enable grpc write coalescing on pool/gw-1 canary.
tyler: i'll draft PRs. also propose a small kernel-selection tweak: prefer minimal-kernel for seq<=8 to shave dispatch overhead for micro requests. That should be quick and safe.
ajay: will add a microbench harness for end-to-end 1-4 token path (include kv cache warm/cold). need baseline numbers before rollouts.
sam: I'll schedule a 1h canary window tonight 02:00-03:00 UTC. will monitor host CPU, kv evictions, p99 latency.
maria: leaving notes for oncall: rollback flags: ingress.fast_path_preparse=false, revert PR#8421, disable grpc-writev-coalesce. ping @oncall if p99 > 200ms.
tyler: :thumbsup: thanks all. I'll push PRs and post links here.
ajay: PRs: 8472 (ascii_quick_scan, flag), 8473 (grpc writev coalesce), 8474 (kernel-pref for short seqs). linking after CI.
maria: great. keep updates short in this thread, thanks!
